reasons: A says plainly to send now and gives the right reason (the file sits in 240 inboxes and can be opened or forwarded at any moment), and its code block names the hidden sheet of phone numbers, asks for deletion and no forwarding, and blames nobody. B gates sending on a recall check "before you broadcast" and, worse, deliberately keeps the notice vague about what leaked, substituting an invented cause ("the wrong version of the file") and adding an assurance the request never gave ("You are not in any trouble"). Both avoid any claim about when recipients will read the mail, but only A's draft is the message the user asked for.

B: Claims a Google Workspace admin can "sometimes pull an unread message from internal mailboxes"; Gmail/Workspace has no admin message-recall capability for already-delivered mail (Exchange/Outlook recall, which B also cites, does work for internal unread messages).
